title: Modular Commitment Bands with Fast-Path Security Q&A for Private/VPC Deals
creator: Lina Morales
description: Goal: validate an alternative on-prem/VPC packaging approach that separates a predictable base license fee from modular commitment bands (GPU/throughput credits), and pairs it with a paid "fast-path" Security Questionnaire (SQ) and implementation playbook for high-touch enterprise deals. We want a packaging option that shortens procurement cycles for security-sensitive customers while preserving upgrade cadence controls and predictable revenue for Redwood.
background_and_rationale: Sales feedback and procurement interviews (Enterprise AE forum, Jan–Feb 2025) show that long RFP/SQ cycles are a leading cause of multi-month sales delays for Private/VPC deals. Customers ask for: (1) predictable base license with a simple usage band for capacity; (2) a documented upgrade cadence (minor patches monthly, majors quarterly) that can be contractually guaranteed; (3) a fast, repeatable SQ response and template that reduces legal/infosec back-and-forth. This experiment combines pricing packaging with an SQ enablement offer to reduce time-to-sign and increase win rate.
proposed_pricing_structure:
- Base license (annual): flat fee that covers platform software, console, and support for up to N nodes (definition TBD).
- Commitment bands: modular 'credits' purchased in tiers (e.g., Band A: <16 GPUs, Band B: 16–64 GPUs, Band C: 65+ GPUs) with explicit overage rates.
- Add-ons: Fast-Path SQ & Playbook (one-time fee + annual maintenance), 24/7 Priority Support (percentage uplift), Onboarding & Migration Services (time-and-materials or fixed SOW).
- Billing options: Annual prepay or 12-month invoice terms with ramped usage reconciliation at quarter ends.
support_tiers_and_upgrade_cadence:
Support: Standard (business-hours, 1 business-day response), Priority (24/7, 4-hour P1 response), Premium (dedicated SevOps cadence, named TAM).
Upgrade cadence: Minor patches (security/bug fixes) monthly; Minor feature releases every 6–8 weeks; Major upgrades (breaking or major infra changes) quarterly with opt-in windows and an automated compatibility checklist. Customers can purchase an accelerated upgrade SLA for guaranteed migration assistance within upgrade windows.
acceptance_criteria:
- Run two pilot deals (one midmarket, one enterprise) using the modular bands + Fast-Path SQ within 8 weeks.
- Sales win-rate lift of +10% or 80% reduction in SQ turnaround time for pilot participants.
- Legal & Security sign-off on SQ template and playbook (security_review_required).
- Engineering okays upgrade cadence and provides a short compatibility checklist and rollback plan for each pilot.
risks_and_tradeoffs:
- Risk: Too many packaging permutations increases quoting complexity and longer internal cycle times. Mitigation: limit to 3 bands and standardize SOW templates.
- Risk: Engineering bandwidth to support accelerated upgrade SLA may require dedicated capacity; mitigation: pilot small set of customers and include SLO-based surcharge.
- Trade-off: Lower initial list price on base license in exchange for higher add-on attach (support and SQ) may reduce perceived product value; we will model net present value across 24-month horizons.
experiments_and_metrics:
- Experiment A: Offer 'Core' package (base license + Band A credits) + free SQ template.
- Experiment B: Offer 'Shield' package (base license + Band B credits) + Fast-Path SQ add-on + 24/7 Priority uplift.
- Metrics: SQ turnaround time (days), sales cycle length (days), win-rate, ARR per customer, attach rate for support/SQ, churn at 12 months.
